claim: Peak memory in distributed MoE training is dominated by the MoE block, not attention: every intermediate buffer in the dispatch pipeline is individually scaled by top-k routing, so a top-8 MoE produces 8x-expanded dispatch tensors.
stance_target: the claim that MoE training memory budgets on 64 GB cards must be computed from top-k expansion, not from parameter count alone
scope_conditions: Qwen3-style MoE, top-8 routing, 4 layers, micro-batch 24, sequence 16384, 8x H100, TP=SP=2, CP=4, EP=8, full recompute
quoted_support: Although SP and CP reduce the number of tokens per GPU entering each MoE block to B x S/(SP x CP) = 49,152, the subsequent top-k expansion multiplies this by 8, producing the dispatch buffers that cause the spikes. As a result, it is the MoE blocks, not attention, that determine the out-of-memory (OOM) boundary for a given training configuration.

claim: Per-layer peak memory during MoE backward exceeds 42 GB on an 80 GB H100 even after attention memory techniques are fully applied, because dispatch and combine stages allocate new outputs while retaining their inputs.
stance_target: the claim that MoE training at long context is memory-bound before it is bandwidth-bound
scope_conditions: Qwen3-style MoE, 8x H100 80 GB, micro-batch 24, sequence 16384, EP=8
quoted_support: These expanded tensors coexist as dispatch and combine stages allocate new outputs while retaining their inputs, driving the per-layer peak above 42 GB during backward.

claim: A ring-based MoE execution model that computes locally as expert weights or tokens circulate avoids full top-k-expanded dispatch buffers and improves full-model training throughput by up to 2.02x at the same GPU memory budget.
stance_target: the claim that MoE training can be made memory-feasible, which matters for whether MoE experiments fit on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: 30B-57B production MoE models; 8 GPUs (2 nodes) and 32 GPUs (8 nodes); H100 64 GB HBM2e, NVLink 4.0 intra-node, NDR InfiniBand inter-node
quoted_support: In full-model training under the same GPU memory budget, it improves throughput by up to 2.02x and extends the largest tested trainable sequence length by up to 2.85x.

claim: RelayMoE's ring dispatch forwards expert weights to ring neighbors via peer-to-peer communication, and cross-node hops use inter-node links, so the mechanism depends on GPU P2P that a no-P2P PCIe box does not provide.
stance_target: the transferability of RelayMoE's mechanism to the CMP 170HX box
quoted_support: At each hop, a GPU computes partial results using its local tokens and the visiting expert partition, accumulates them into the output, and forwards the expert weights to its ring neighbor via peer-to-peer communication.

claim: Frontier MoE architectures have grown dispatch-buffer multipliers from 2x (Mixtral 8x22B, top-2) to 8-10x (DeepSeek-V3 top-8, Qwen3-30B-A3B top-8, newer models top-10), while context lengths grew from 32K to 262K, so MoE dispatch peak memory has grown by an order of magnitude.
stance_target: the claim that MoE memory cost is a moving target that gets worse with each architecture generation
quoted_support: Combined with growing sequence lengths (32K to 262K), peak memory from MoE dispatch has grown by an order of magnitude.

claim: RelayMoE selects between expert routing and token routing according to communication volume, and overlaps transfers with computation, so the ring adapts to whichever direction moves less data.
stance_target: whether a ring schedule can be made bandwidth-aware on a slow fabric
quoted_support: RelayMoE selects between expert and token routing according to communication volume and overlaps transfers with computation.
